```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
have_tm <- all(vapply(c("tune", "workflows", "recipes", "rsample", "yardstick", "dials"),
                      requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_tm)
```

**plsnip** adds the engine `"pls"` to `parsnip::pls()`. Models are fitted with
the [pls](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pls) package, so they behave
exactly like `pls::plsr()`, but they can be used in recipes, workflows,
resampling and tuning. The engine is registered when the package is loaded.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(plsnip)       # attaches parsnip
library(recipes)
library(workflows)
library(rsample)
library(tune)
library(yardstick)
library(dials)
```

Remember `set_engine("pls")`: the default engine of `pls()` is `"mixOmics"`.

## Regression: octane from NIR spectra

```{r}
data(gasoline, package = "pls")
gas <- data.frame(octane = gasoline$octane, unclass(gasoline$NIR))
dim(gas)

set.seed(1)
split <- initial_split(gas, prop = 0.75)
folds <- vfold_cv(training(split), v = 5)

pls_reg <- pls(num_comp = tune()) |>
  set_engine("pls") |>          # kernel PLS, predictors centred (not scaled)
  set_mode("regression")

wf_reg <- workflow(recipe(octane ~ ., data = gas), pls_reg)
```

`num_comp` is a *submodel* parameter: each resample is fitted once with the
largest number of components and predictions for the smaller numbers come from
the same fit, so a grid of 15 values costs 5 fits here. The default range of
`dials::num_comp()` is 1–4, so give it a wider one.

```{r}
res_reg <- tune_grid(wf_reg, folds,
                     grid = grid_regular(num_comp(range = c(1, 15)), levels = 15),
                     metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq),
                     control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE))
show_best(res_reg, metric = "rmse", n = 3)
autoplot(res_reg)
```

### Cross-validated Q² as in `pls`

`collect_metrics()` averages each metric over the folds, and yardstick's `rsq`
is a squared correlation. The Q² reported by `pls::R2(fit, estimate = "CV")`
is instead pooled over all held-out predictions, `1 - PRESS / SS`. It can be
computed from the saved predictions:

```{r}
q2 <- collect_predictions(res_reg) |>
  dplyr::group_by(num_comp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(rmsep = sqrt(mean((octane - .pred)^2)),
                   q2 = 1 - sum((octane - .pred)^2) / sum((octane - mean(octane))^2))
q2[q2$num_comp %in% 1:6, ]
```

### Final model

```{r}
final_reg <- finalize_workflow(wf_reg, select_best(res_reg, metric = "rmse")) |>
  last_fit(split)
collect_metrics(final_reg)
```

The engine object is an ordinary `mvr` object, so the pls tools work on it:

```{r}
mvr_fit <- extract_fit_engine(final_reg)
class(mvr_fit)
pls::explvar(mvr_fit)
plot(seq(900, 1700, by = 2), coef(mvr_fit), type = "l",
     xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Regression coefficient")
```

## Classification (PLS-DA): oil type of mayonnaise

```{r}
data(mayonnaise, package = "pls")
mayo <- data.frame(oil = factor(paste0("oil", mayonnaise$oil.type)),
                   unclass(mayonnaise$NIR))
table(mayo$oil)
```

The outcome is coded as one dummy column per class and a single PLS2 model is
fitted. Class probabilities come from LDA on the PLS scores (default,
`prob_method = "lda"`) or from a softmax of the predicted dummies
(`prob_method = "softmax"`, useful only for ranking metrics such as ROC AUC).

```{r}
pls_cls <- pls(num_comp = tune()) |>
  set_engine("pls", prob_method = "lda") |>
  set_mode("classification")

set.seed(2)
folds_cls <- vfold_cv(mayo, v = 5, strata = oil)
res_cls <- tune_grid(workflow(recipe(oil ~ ., data = mayo), pls_cls), folds_cls,
                     grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:12),
                     metrics = metric_set(accuracy, roc_auc, mn_log_loss))
show_best(res_cls, metric = "accuracy", n = 3)
```

Predictions for several numbers of components from one fit:

```{r}
fit_cls <- pls(num_comp = 8) |>
  set_engine("pls") |>
  set_mode("classification") |>
  fit(oil ~ ., data = mayo)
predict(fit_cls, mayo[1:3, ], type = "prob")
multi_predict(fit_cls, mayo[1, ], type = "class", num_comp = c(2, 4, 8))$.pred[[1]]
```

## Engine arguments

* `method`: `"kernelpls"` (default), `"widekernelpls"`, `"simpls"`,
  `"oscorespls"`.
* `scale`: scale predictors to unit variance (default `FALSE`).
* `prob_method`: `"lda"` (default) or `"softmax"`, classification only.
* any other argument of `pls::mvr()`.

`predictor_prop` (sparse PLS) is not available; use the `"mixOmics"` engine
for that. See `?details_pls_pls` for details.
